chunks: From Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan, he said: I heard Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) saying:

Indeed, Allah (Glorified is His Majesty) has among His creatures some servants; whenever an affliction descends from the heavens or a deficiency in sustenance occurs, He drives it towards them, and whenever there is well-being or ample sustenance, He diverts it from them. And if the light of one of them were divided among all the inhabitants of the earth, it would suffice them.
ai.seo_question: Why do the righteous bear afflictions while others enjoy ease?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the unique spiritual status of Allah's special servants (often interpreted as the Imams or the righteous), explaining that they bear the brunt of afflictions and scarcity so that others may enjoy ease and abundance. Their spiritual light is so profound that if distributed among all people, it would be sufficient for everyone.

en.muhajir-b-ali: 23. It has been narrated that Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan said: I heard Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s) saying:

Indeed, Allah has amongst His creatures some (special) servants; whenever an affliction descends from the heavens or a deficiency in sustenance, He drives it towards them. And whenever (there is) well-being or ample sustenance, He diverts it from them. (And) if the light (nur) of one of them were to be divided between all the inhabitants of the earth, it would suffice them.
